title: How Contract Law Built the Blockchain (Class 3.2)
takeaways: Paper contracts serve as static specifications; smart contracts operate as active runtime state machines.
Nick Szabo solved the validator incentive problem by embedding gas fees into network state transitions as programmatic legal consideration.
Ricardian contracts cryptographically bind human-readable prose with machine-readable software hashes.
Alonzo Church's lambda calculus proves that written text itself serves as a universal functional computing interface for legal specs.
Regulated stablecoins (USDC) preserve judicial enforcement and freeze functions, whereas bridged tokens (USDCE) rely on L2 bridge contracts restricting traditional court remedies.
